# Daylight Savings Time and Fatal Crashes

There is ongoing debate over whether the United States should continue
with its current practice of moving clocks one hour ahead in early
March and one hour back in early November, in other words to observe
``daylight savings time'' during the middle of the year. The U.S.\
House of Representatives has passed a bill to place the country on 
permanent daylight savings time. Others propose that we switch to
permanent standard time, which means not altering the clocks at all.

Your task in this project is to produce statistical analyses that
attempt to answer the question, "What is the effect of daylight
savings on traffic fatalities in the U.S.?" The challenge here is that
we have not run controlled experiments, so we must try to answer the
question using observational data.

You have been provided with a dataset called ``fars.RData'', which has
10 years of data from the Fatality Analysis Reporting System,
a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration program for collecting
fatal accident reports into a national database. The data go back to 1975;
additional data beyond the 10 years provided can be found here:

https://www.nhtsa.gov/file-downloads?p=nhtsa/downloads/FARS/

You may use this dataset or any external datasets to help answer the
project question. In additional to the project question, your group
should propose another interesting question and attempt to answer
it using a statistical analysis.
